entities.summary: Gaito Gazdanov Russian: Гайто́ Газда́нов; Ossetian: Гӕздӕнты Гайто; 6 December [O.S. 23 November] 1902 – 5 December 1971) was a Russian émigré writer of Ossetian descent, who lived in Paris. Gazdanov's first stories were published in France in 1926 in Russian. His novels An Evening with Claire (1929) and The Spectre of Alexander Wolf (1948) became his most well-known works, mentioned by writers Maxim Gorky, Ivan Bunin and Vladislav Khodasevich. Gazdanov was a member of the French Resistance in occupied France.
